holidays.name: National 7-Eleven Day (Free Slurpee Day)
holidays.description: Brain freeze, assemble! Every July 11 (7/11), the convenience-store giant celebrates its own name with free Slurpees. Fans line up for a free small cup of the icy, swirly drink.
holidays.origin: The date works because 7/11 matches the chain's name. The company began in 1927 as Tote'm Stores in Dallas, Texas. It became 7-Eleven in 1946, after it extended its hours to 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. The free-Slurpee tradition grew out of birthday celebrations for the brand.
holidays.funFact: The name '7-Eleven' came from the store's once-shocking long opening hours, which were unusual in the 1940s.

holidays.name: Cheer Up the Lonely Day
holidays.description: A day for brightening the day of someone who may be feeling isolated. You could send a note, make a phone call, or invite a neighbor for coffee. The goal is to remind someone they matter.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular fixture on July calendars as a reminder to reach out to people who feel alone.
holidays.funFact: A small gesture can go a long way. Research on social connection shows that even brief friendly contact can lift a person's mood.

holidays.name: Bowdler's Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day for the art of editing out the naughty bits. It's named after the man who scrubbed Shakespeare clean for polite Victorian readers. Celebrate by censoring your favorite book or by reading one that was censored.
holidays.origin: The day honors Thomas Bowdler, born July 11, 1754. He published 'The Family Shakespeare' in 1807, with the parts he considered unsuitable for families removed.
holidays.funFact: Bowdler's work gave English the verb 'bowdlerize', which means to remove material considered offensive from a text.
